source.reason: The original 315-byte hand-authored Matroska metadata stub: a 3840x2160 HEVC track declared through CodecPrivate and a Dolby Vision BlockAdditionMapping with no decodable frames. FFmpeg writes those elements only around a real encoded stream. The configuration-record path is covered by dv_profile5.mkv (FFmpeg plus dvcC insertion, then an FFmpeg remux); exact stub bytes belong in the crate's own in-code builders, as the original suite's sparse_mkv support did.
Hand-authored metadata stub, as stubs/dv_profile5.mkv; covered by dv_profile7.mkv.
Hand-authored metadata stub, as stubs/dv_profile5.mkv; covered by dv_profile8.mkv.

The original 283-byte hand-authored stub: a 3840x2160 HEVC track whose only frame is an SEI carrying ITU-T T.35 HDR10+ metadata. Covered by hevc_hdr10plus.mkv, a real libx265 encode with dhdr10-info metadata.
The original 691-byte hand-authored MP4 stub of the same shape; covered by hevc_hdr10plus.mp4.
No VVC (H.266) encoder: the FFmpeg 8.1.1 build used to author the corpus does not link libvvenc, and no other encoder is allowed.
HE-AAC (SBR) needs libfdk_aac, which the FFmpeg 8.1.1 build used to author the corpus does not link; the native AAC encoder writes LC only.
HE-AACv2 (SBR + PS): as audio/he_aac_v1.m4a.
FFmpeg 8.1.1's native AAC encoder refuses the Main profile ("Profile not supported"); libfdk_aac is not linked.
FFmpeg 8.1.1's native AAC encoder refuses the LTP profile ("Profile not supported"); libfdk_aac is not linked.
AMR-NB needs libopencore-amrnb, which the FFmpeg 8.1.1 build used to author the corpus does not link.
AMR-WB needs libvo-amrwbenc, which the FFmpeg 8.1.1 build used to author the corpus does not link.
No encoder writes Dolby Atmos (E-AC-3 JOC); FFmpeg's E-AC-3 encoder writes no object audio, and the JOC extension cannot be authored honestly without a reference bitstream.
FFmpeg's TrueHD encoder writes no Atmos substream; as audio/eac3_joc_atmos.mp4.
FFmpeg's DTS encoder writes the core only; DTS-HD MA, HRA, ES, 96/24, DTS:X and DTS Express extensions have no encoder.
FFmpeg has a WMA Pro decoder but no encoder.
FFmpeg has a WMA Lossless decoder but no encoder.
FFmpeg has VC-1 / WMV3 decoders but no encoder.
FFmpeg has a Sorenson Video 3 decoder but no encoder.
FFmpeg's dvdsub encoder needs bitmap subtitle input, and nothing allowed here produces bitmap subtitles (FFmpeg cannot render text subtitles to bitmaps).
FFmpeg has no PGS (HDMV presentation graphics) encoder.
As subtitle/dvdsub.mkv: the DVB subtitle encoder needs bitmap input.
AV1 High (4:4:4) and Professional profiles: SVT-AV1, the only AV1 encoder linked here, writes Main profile only.
Matroska has no dvwC block-addition mapping that FFmpeg writes; the dvwC path is covered in MP4.
FFmpeg's Matroska muxer writes no ContentEncryption elements.

Asked for -profile:v mainstillpicture (or msp) on a single 4:2:0 8-bit frame, the libx265 in the FFmpeg 8.1.1 build used to author the corpus writes general_profile_idc 4 (Format Range Extensions), not 3.
FFmpeg 8.1.1's TS muxer has no AV1 mapping: it writes the stream as private data that no demuxer reads as AV1. Covers every AV1-in-TS shape (av1_pq_no_static.ts, av1_hlg.ts, av1_hdr10plus.ts).
AV1 in TS, as hdr/av1_hdr10.ts.
FFmpeg's MOV muxer refuses VP8.
FFmpeg's MPEG-4 encoder has no global motion compensation.
FFmpeg's Ogg muxer refuses Dirac / VC-2.
Ogg video needs Theora or Dirac; covered audio-only by lang/iso639_2_ita.ogg.
FFmpeg's m2ts mode allows one program (as Blu-ray does); two programs are covered in 188-byte TS by program/two_programs.ts.

builders.notes: OGM (DirectShow stream headers inside Ogg), which no FFmpeg muxer writes. The Vorbis headers inside come from an FFmpeg-encoded Ogg Vorbis stream.

coverage.notes: One fixture per classifying branch of the parser: HDR10, PQ without static metadata, HLG and HDR10+ in HEVC, AV1, VP9 and H.264; Dolby Vision profiles 5, 7, 8.1, 8.2, 8.4, 9 and 10 signalled through dvcC/dvvC/dvwC, Matroska BlockAdditionMapping, the TS DOVI descriptor and RPU NAL units; codec profiles, bit depths and chroma formats; audio codecs, layouts and profiles; subtitle formats; dispositions; language tags; chapters, attachments, cover art and captions; geometry (aspect ratios, rotation, interlacing, stereo 3D, variable frame rate); multi-program TS; and encrypted or scrambled payloads. Signals no encoder writes are authored in Rust after the encode: SEI messages, Dolby Vision RPU NAL units and configuration boxes, AV1 ITU-T T.35 metadata OBUs, A/53 caption user data and scrambling bits (xtask/src/recipes/inject.rs).

disc.notes: DVD-Video ISO 9660 images (VIDEO_TS IFO navigation around an FFmpeg MPEG-2 program stream) and Blu-ray / UHD Blu-ray UDF 2.50 / 2.60 images (BDMV index, MovieObject, MPLS playlist and CLPI clip information around FFmpeg M2TS clips), written by xtask/src/recipes/disc.rs.

dolby_vision.notes: HEVC Main 10 PQ from libx265 with a dvcC box inserted into the hvc1 sample entry by Rust after FFmpeg; the Matroska variants are FFmpeg remuxes of those MP4s, which carry the record into BlockAdditionMapping. There is no RPU in the bitstream: the fixtures test the configuration record, not RPU parsing.

imported.notes: Files read byte for byte from the public repository the parser was extracted from, at a pinned commit, and checked against a pinned size and BLAKE3. The parser's own tests assert facts of these exact bytes, which a regenerated file does not reproduce. Not generated, so not byte-reproducible from a recipe.

large.notes: Budget fixtures: an MP4 whose moov is larger than the 64 MiB read budget, an MP4 with a four-million-entry sample table, a Matroska live stream with no cues and unknown-size clusters, and a long interleaved MPEG-TS.

matrix.notes: testsrc2 video and silent anullsrc audio across MKV, WebM, MP4/M4V/MOV, AVI, TS/M2TS, ASF, Ogg and FLV. Two TS fixtures re-frame another fixture's packets into 192- and 204-byte packets, and one ASF fixture has its PCM format rewritten to WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE, both in Rust after FFmpeg. simd_scan_dense.bin is written by Rust: it is scanner input, not media.

supplemental.notes: AV1, HEVC HDR10/HLG/HDR10+ (x265 SEI and dhdr10-info), PQ sequence headers, Nero and QuickTime chapters, MPEG-1/2 program streams and an 8K H.264 stream.

synthesized.notes: Files past 1, 2 and 4 GiB written by Rust from an imported seed and format padding (an MP4 mdat, an EBML Void, null TS packets, an AVI JUNK chunk), sparse where the format allows. Never published: hydrate writes them from the seed and checks the size and BLAKE3 the recipe pins, so the bytes are reproducible.
